rows: The writer uses personification. Engines cough and die.
The engines 'cough and die', so the harbour sounds like a tired, ill old man: the verb 'cough' makes the boats seem human, struggling to breathe at the end of a long day.

blocks.h: Model PETZAAL paragraph: If I Must Die

passage.title: Model paragraph
paras: Alareer presents his death as the start of someone else's hope. The closing lines, 'If I must die, / you must live / to tell my story', repeat the command 'let it', so the speaker gives his story away like a gift. The verb 'bring' suggests the story will travel to others, and 'tale' turns a life into something to be told again. An alternative reading is that the repetition is a plea as much as a command. Writing in Gaza, Alareer insists that a story outlives the person who tells it.
